question: Two roommates, Isaac and Nora, tracked shared grocery funds, and Nora's contribution always trailed his. Isaac put in 57 dollars at the start of the month. He added 73 more dollars from his paycheck. He then spent 12 dollars on cleaning supplies. A refund doubled his remaining balance. The balance was then split evenly between 2 joint accounts, and only one account was tracked. A late deposit added 34 more dollars. A rent payment took out 137 dollars. How much money was left in that account?

A hardware store began the morning with 187 hammers in stock. By midmorning, 9 more hammers arrived from a supplier. At midday, 66 more hammers came in from a second shipment. In the afternoon, 6 more hammers were added from a returned order. A weekend sale required the store to prepare 3 times that afternoon total. How many hammers did the store prepare for the sale?

A theater sold 200 tickets by the morning box office opening. By midday, 141 tickets had to be refunded after a show was postponed, and an afternoon promotion made the remaining tickets grow to 5 times its size. Since the box office counts tickets individually but the accountant reports revenue in whole dollars, the manager kept both figures on separate sheets. That evening, 164 more tickets were refunded for a second cancellation. A late rebooking event made that total grow to 3 times its size. Overnight, 45 tickets were voided due to a printing error, and a final morning rush made the remaining tickets grow to 7 times its size. How many tickets did the theater have after that final rush?

A charity walk began with 58 dollars pledged at sign-up, while a separate fun run nearby collected 500 water bottles for its own runners, unrelated to this event. During the walk, 46 dollars had to be refunded to a canceled participant. A bake sale table added 3 more dollars, and a raffle added 20 more dollars. A matching gift added 6 more dollars. A late donor added 39 more dollars. A final pledge added 69 more dollars. How much money had the walk raised in total?

Two shop owners, Bettina and Marcus, tracked shoe inventory, and Marcus's stock always trailed hers. Bettina's shop had 225 pairs of shoes at the season's start, and a wholesale deal doubled her stock right away. She then returned 78 pairs that didn't sell. A new shipment made her remaining stock grow to 4 times its size, and a second shipment made it grow to 2 times its size again, while the mall's food court reported selling 3000 pretzels that same week, unrelated to shoes. A clearance event removed 1121 pairs sold at a discount. A final donation removed 1099 more pairs given to a charity. How many pairs of shoes were left in Bettina's shop?

A charity car wash began the morning with 122 dollars collected. By midmorning, 71 more dollars came in. A matching pledge doubled that total. In the afternoon, 68 more dollars were added from a bake sale table. That evening, 423 dollars had to be paid out for equipment rental. Overnight, 25 more dollars were spent on cleanup supplies. A final morning bonus made the remaining total grow to 5 times its size. How much money did the car wash have after that bonus?

Two clerks, Odalys and Bram, tracked register cash, and Bram's drawer always held less than hers. Odalys's drawer started the shift with 105 dollars. She paid out 58 dollars in change to a customer. She then paid out 24 more dollars for a return. A tip jar added 43 more dollars. Since the register logs everything in dollars and cents but the nightly report rounds to the nearest dollar, Odalys always double-checked the total. Her remaining cash was split evenly across 6 deposit bags, and only one bag was tracked. How much money was in that bag?

Two roommates, Priya and Elias, tracked their shared snack fund, and Elias's contribution always fell behind hers. Priya put in 232 dollars at the start of the semester. She spent 104 dollars restocking the pantry. She then spent 70 more dollars on a bulk grocery run, unrelated to the 15 unopened boxes of napkins stacked in the closet. A refund added 30 more dollars. A bonus from a roommate's parent made the remaining total grow to 5 times its size. A final grocery bill cost 283 dollars. How much money was left in the snack fund?

Two artists, Lucia and Faron, tracked mural paint cans, and Faron always used fewer cans than she did. Lucia started the morning with 189 cans of paint, while a dozen empty cans from an old project sat unused in the corner. By midmorning, 2 cans were used up finishing a background. In the afternoon, 62 more cans arrived from a supplier. That evening, her stock was organized into 8 identical crates, each holding that same amount, for a citywide mural project. Overnight, 720 cans were used across the city for the project. How many cans were left after the project?

A print shop began the morning with 54 posters ready. By midday, that stack was multiplied across 8 identical print runs, each producing that same amount, for a citywide campaign. In the afternoon, a second campaign made that total grow to 2 times its size. By evening, a bulk client order required the total to grow to 9 times its size. Overnight, the shipment was split evenly across 4 delivery trucks, and only one truck's load was tracked. How many posters were on that truck?

A café started the morning with 155 cups of coffee sold. By midmorning, 23 more cups were sold. At midday, a catering order required the café to prepare 3 times that morning total. Since the café measures coffee grounds in ounces but sells drinks by the cup, the barista kept a conversion chart on the wall. In the afternoon, a citywide event required 8 times that midday total. By evening, 13 more cups were sold at a pop-up stand. How many cups had the café sold by evening?

A charity bake sale began the morning with 201 cookies on the table. By midmorning, 29 more cookies were added from a late batch. Unrelated to cookies, a neighboring stand sold 400 balloons that same morning. In the afternoon, 194 cookies were sold to a large school group. The remaining cookies were split evenly across 3 trays, and only one tray was tracked. That evening, a matching order required that tray's cookies to grow to 5 times its size. How many cookies were needed for that evening order?

A toy store began the morning with 226 puzzle boxes on the shelf. A wholesale order removed 106 boxes. Unrelated to puzzles, a nearby craft store restocked 800 rolls of ribbon that same morning. A clearance sale removed 95 more boxes. A donation added 9 more boxes. A late shipment added 31 more boxes. A regional order required the store to prepare 4 times that total. How many puzzle boxes did the store need for the regional order?

A charity bake sale multiplied its opening total of 131 dollars across 5 identical volunteer tables, each collecting that same amount, combining into one grand total. A late donation added 36 more dollars. A matching-gift program made that total grow to 5 times its size. The final total was then split evenly among 5 school clubs, and only one club's share was tracked. How much money did that club receive?

A factory began the morning with 6 identical machines, each producing 155 parts, combined into one production total. By midday, a second production line made that total grow to 3 times its size. In the afternoon, a third batch made it grow to 5 times its size. By evening, a final rush order made it grow to 6 times its size. Overnight, the entire shipment was split evenly between 2 warehouses, and only one warehouse's stock was tracked. How many parts were in that warehouse the next morning?

Two savers, Odalys and Winston, tracked their coin banks, and Winston's bank always held less than hers. Odalys's bank held 135 dollars at the start of the month. She spent 58 dollars on a birthday gift. She then earned 69 more dollars mowing lawns. She then earned 13 more dollars from a garage sale. A matching bonus from her uncle doubled her remaining total. How much money was in Odalys's bank after the bonus?

A juice stand started the morning with 35 cups sold. By midmorning, 9 cups had to be remade after a spill. By midday, 6 more cups were lost to a broken blender. The remaining cups were split evenly across 4 volunteers, and only one volunteer's count was tracked. In the afternoon, that volunteer sold 30 more cups. How many cups had that volunteer sold by afternoon?

A theater sold 119 tickets by the start of the week. On Tuesday, 109 tickets were refunded after a show was rescheduled. On Wednesday, 67 more tickets were sold. On Thursday, 64 more tickets were sold. On Friday, 41 more tickets were sold. Since the box office counts tickets but the accountant reports revenue in cents rather than tickets, the manager kept a separate ledger. On Saturday, 7 tickets were voided due to a printing error, and a final matching promotion tripled the remaining total. How many tickets did the theater end up with?

A candy factory began the day with 9 identical machines, each producing 158 gumballs, combined into one batch. That batch was then multiplied across 8 identical packaging lines, each handling that same amount, for a bulk shipment. A separate machine down the hall, unrelated to gumballs, produced 500 chocolate bars that same day. A late addition brought 35 more gumballs into the shipment total. Since the factory counts gumballs individually but the invoice bills by weight in ounces, the shipping clerk always converted the numbers. A recall then removed 7054 gumballs found to be defective. How many gumballs were left after the recall?

A bakery began the morning with 4 identical ovens, each holding 58 rolls, combined into one batch. By midmorning, 128 rolls were sold to a wholesale client. A lunch rush made the remaining rolls grow to 5 times their size. Since the bakery weighs flour in ounces but sells rolls by count, the baker kept two separate ledgers. In the afternoon, 232 rolls were donated to a shelter. By evening, 156 more rolls were given away at a community event. Overnight, a final order made the remaining total grow to 6 times its size. How many rolls were ready by the next morning?

A recycling center started Monday with 177 pounds of cans collected, unrelated to the 250 plastic bottles gathered separately that day. The cans were then split evenly across 3 collection bins, and only one bin's total was tracked. A Tuesday drive added 68 more pounds to that bin. A Wednesday drive added 27 more pounds. A regional order required that bin's total to grow to 9 times its size. How many pounds of cans were needed for the regional order?

A trading card shop began the morning with 61 rare cards in the vault, while a dozen employees clocked in for inventory day, unrelated to the count. The stock was multiplied across 9 identical display cases, each holding that same amount, for a convention. A second expansion required 5 times that convention total for a pop-up booth. A third expansion required 9 times that new total for a second booth. A fourth expansion required 5 times that amount for a third booth. Afterward, 118425 cards had to be returned to the warehouse after the convention closed. How many cards were left in the vault?

Two clerks, Josefina and Dwayne, tracked register minutes worked, and Dwayne always logged fewer than she did. Josefina logged 172 minutes at the start of her shift, unrelated to the 500 receipts printed that day. She then lost 122 minutes to an unpaid break. A late bonus added 4 more minutes. Since the timesheet logs minutes but payroll reports hours, Josefina always converted the number before submitting it. Her remaining minutes were split evenly across 3 pay periods, and only one period was tracked. That period's minutes were then split evenly between 2 weeks, and only one week was tracked. How many minutes did that week show?

A food bank started the morning with 194 pounds of pasta in storage, unrelated to the 300 cans of soup donated separately that day. By midmorning, 28 pounds were distributed to local families. A grocery store donated 49 more pounds. A farm delivered 46 more pounds. Since the food bank logs weight in pounds but its national report converts everything to kilograms, staff always double-checked the numbers. By afternoon, 230 pounds were sent to a partner shelter. A final matching donation made the remaining total grow to 6 times its size. How many pounds of pasta were left after that donation?

Two friends, Marisol and Dante, tracked seashell counts, and Dante always found fewer than she did. Marisol collected 150 shells on the first day, unrelated to the 400 grains of sand she measured just for fun. She then lost 131 shells when a wave swept her bag away, 2 more shells to a crab, and 1 more shell in the sand. She then gave away 4 shells to a younger child. Her remaining shells were split evenly between 2 jars, and only one jar was tracked. That jar then lost 3 more shells to a crack. How many shells were in that jar?
